Create a rough pie chart

Source: R/roughViz.R
roughPie.Rd

Thin wrapper around [roughDonut()] that renders slices without the hollow centre.

Usage

roughPie(
  data,
  labels = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  roughness = 1,
  fillStyle = "hachure",
  fillWeight = NULL,
  strokeWidth = 1,
  bowing = 0,
  simplification = 0,
  font = 0,
  margin = NULL,
  legend = TRUE,
  legendPosition = "right",
  titleAlign = "center",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A `data.frame` or named list. With a data frame you must supply column names via `labels` and `values`. With a list the expected structure is `list(labels = <character>, values = <numeric>)`.

labels

String giving the column name used for labels when `data` is a data frame.

values

String naming the column that contains numeric values when `data` is a data frame.

title

Optional chart heading.

width

Optional width of the widget (pixels or CSS lengths).

height

Optional height of the widget (pixels or CSS lengths).

colors

Character vector of fill colours. Leave `NULL` to let the library choose defaults.

roughness

Roughness level forwarded to roughViz.js.

fillStyle

Fill style, such as `"hachure"` or `"zigzag"`.

fillWeight

Thickness of the fill pattern strokes.

strokeWidth

Width of the slice outlines.

bowing

Amount of curvature applied to straight lines.

simplification

Simplification tolerance for curves.

font

Font family reference (`0`, `1`, or custom name).

margin

Named list describing the plot margins.

legend

Logical flag controlling whether the legend is rendered.

legendPosition

Position of the legend (`"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, or `"right"`).

titleAlign

Horizontal alignment of the title (`"left"`, `"center"`, or `"right"`).

...

Additional named options forwarded to the underlying JavaScript widget.

Value

A pie chart `htmlwidget`.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  roughPie(
    data = data.frame(
      labels = c("A", "B", "C"),
      values = c(40, 35, 25)
    ),
    labels = "labels",
    values = "values",
    title = "Share of responses"
  )
}
